sed.note: Repeated stdin and final-newline preservation are fixed. Regex and per-file state differ from GNU; an evaluated dollar address before early pipe quit can consume one lookahead byte.

nl.note: Repeated stdin, stale stream read-ahead and named-file descriptor ownership are fixed. BRE matching uses the host regex library; without REG_STARTEND, patterns cannot match past embedded NUL bytes.

pr.note: Repeated stdin, paging and output failures are fixed for the tested subset. Numbered multi-column control bytes, merged unterminated records and several GNU options remain documented exclusions.

tac.next: Decide bounded-memory input and GNU regex scope; see the tac follow-up.

fold.note: Buffered ASCII processing is validated; the existing permissive UTF-8 decoder and short-input fread lookahead behavior remain. Unicode and appliance throughput are not established.

expand.note: Buffered output and per-invocation input are validated. Documented option/tab-stop differences and locale scope remain; tiny-input speedup is not established.

diff.note: Minus operands denote stdin, including diff - -. Dedicated fixtures compare edit addresses and final newlines with GNU and exercise allocation failures. The historical timing case uses identical files.

unexpand.note: Write-failure stop and GNU comparison are covered by tests/unexpand-check.sh.

wc.note: Requested word-count assertions are covered by tests/wc-check.sh and tests/wc-tail-parity.sh.

comm.note: Selected-column GNU comparisons and write-failure contracts have a dedicated regression. The historical 2026-09-12 comm case measured 0.50 times the external runtime; current performance needs a new measurement.

join.note: Write-failure stop and GNU comparison are covered by tests/join-check.sh.

sort.note: Write-failure handling and selected GNU comparisons have dedicated regressions. The historical 2026-09-12 sort-text case measured 0.91 times the external runtime; it is not an open confirmed performance defect.

crypto.note: Failed writes return failure. Dedicated state fixtures cover handle cleanup, output binding and subsequent invocations.

rev.note: Write-failure stop and GNU comparison are covered by tests/rev-check.sh.

col.note: Repeated redirected stdin is fixed; tests/col-check.sh matches GNU on three fresh redirections. Output is newline-terminated as util-linux does, including an unterminated final line, which is what the large text fixture has. File operands are a bash-os extension: util-linux col reads stdin only and rejects an operand, so that path has no reference.

split.note: Repeated redirected input has dedicated comparisons; private fixtures also cover piece contents, input aliases and output failures.

csplit.note: Repeated redirected stdin is fixed; tests/csplit-check.sh matches GNU piece files across three redirections.

tee.note: Closed-stdin and all-outputs-failed stop are covered by tests/tee-check.sh. Stock examples/loadables/tee.c is still the source.

tail.note: Repeated small-input redirections and write-error stop are covered by tests/tail-check.sh.

ar.note: Truncated headers, extract write errors and short member bodies are rejected; tests/ar-check.sh matches GNU 2.44 including /dev/full unlink and archive-link identity.

du.note: A failed size-report write now returns failure; tests/du-check.sh covers du -b file > /dev/full.

mv.note: Self-moves fail without changing bytes. Additional fixtures cover long paths, cross-filesystem moves, modes and injected close/metadata failures.

truncate.note: Size arithmetic overflow is rejected and existing bytes are preserved; tests/truncate-check.sh matches GNU.

cp.note: An unreadable source preserves an existing destination. Additional fixtures cover recursive bounds, aliases, metadata and close failures; selected GNU comparisons are mapped in the CSV.

zstd.note: Default-level stdin compress/decompress is ahead of host zstd(1) on the catalog binary; frames are not byte-identical and validation is round-trip. BusyBox has no applet. Whole-file reads and one-shot ZSTD_compress remain.
zstd.next: See the dedicated zstd report; extend sizes and levels if a slower case appears.

hostid.note: Default is gethostid(3), matching hostid(1), including on this measured full binary. tests/hostid-check.sh covers override files and the machine-id fallback.

free.note: Measured against a pinned /proc via BASHOS_PROC_ROOT, self-timed: the live counters move between the reference call and the repeated batch, so a live ratio could only ever fail. tests/free-check.sh holds the GNU parity.

coreutils.note: Dispatcher; each subcommand is measured separately. nproc's default counts the affinity mask, as GNU's does, so it follows a taskset pin; --all reports every configured processor. GNU's OMP_NUM_THREADS and OMP_THREAD_LIMIT overrides are deliberately not implemented.

mktemp.note: The former -u create-then-unlink defect is fixed: name-only generation leaves the filesystem untouched. The regression also covers ordinary file and directory creation.

passwd.note: Empty passwd fields retain their column positions in list and lookup paths; dedicated fixtures cover empty and malformed records. The historical timing fixture remains unchanged.

vi.note: After `dd` deletes the buffer's last line the cursor is left on a line that no longer exists, and every later `dd` is a silent no-op returning 0; nvim clamps the cursor and keeps deleting. The benchmark fixture deliberately omits `G` before its dd run: with it the case would have measured one edit instead of 250 while still validating.
vi.next: Clamp the cursor to the new last line after a delete.

dmesg.note: The former split-record loss is fixed. Fixture checks cover records crossing read boundaries and an unterminated final record; device fixtures also exercise input bounds.

fstrim.note: `-I/--listed-in` reports, and would trim, any path in the list file that merely stat()s; util-linux cross-checks each entry against the live mount table and reports only mounted filesystems. This is why the case is self-timed: there is no output to compare against util-linux, which exits non-zero on the same input.

rsync.note: For a non-existent single-file DEST the builtin creates the destination as a directory, while stock rsync treats DEST as a directory only when it already exists or ends in '/'. The measured case uses the trailing-slash form into a reset-recreated directory, where the two agree byte for byte.

lsattr.note: The flag field is 14 columns where e2fsprogs prints 22 for the same file, so the two cannot be compared on exact bytes.

obj.note: The getline(stdin) loops now clearerr(stdin) at the builtin entry: without it a second in-process `--batch-check`, `--batch`, `hash --stdin-paths` or `tree` emitted nothing while still exiting 0, because a builtin does not fork and the stream keeps its EOF flag.

bsdgames.note: The headless games read stdin with fgets and now clearerr(stdin) at the builtin entry; before, a second game in the same shell read nothing and exited 0 without playing.

ts.note: Capture precedence takes the last matching pattern rather than the most specific: in span mode a JSON object key yields both string.special.key and string, and the renderer paints it with the later, less specific rule.

git.note: The recorded parity run covers 69 scenarios and 414 comparisons. Dedicated integrity and apply-path regressions cover malformed storage, preflight failures, complete long patch lines and nested rename strip levels; this is not full Git compatibility.

pkg.note: Index verification uses the same byte buffer that is published. Separate trust and package-publication fixtures cover signature lookup, trust-file failures and install rollback, including sanitizer checks.

vt.note: Dedicated edge fixtures cover drained response cloning, complete combining sequences in diff/scrollback output and bounded CSI numeric parsing.

buf.note: Dedicated edge fixtures cover reload cleanup and saving through an aliased retained filename.

expect.note: A continuous-output child cannot extend the whole-wait deadline; the regression uses a private PTY.

ptybroker.note: Private PTY fixtures cover broker lifecycle, binary I/O, backpressure and screen attachment. No broad command benchmark is recorded.

validation.summary: At measurement time, the full catalog contained 279 entries: 248 had individual command timings and 31 did not. The batch used seven samples per case, pinned to one CPU under the shared benchmark lock. The measured binary includes repeated-input fixes for more, less, uuencode, xargs, obj and bsdgames, affinity-aware coreutils nproc, and col output termination. The full test harness was not rerun for that measurement batch.

ci_followup: Historical [CI at 5fde494](https://github.com/itsmygithubacct/bash-os/actions/runs/34214029478) passed all nine jobs on the pre-integration tree. The integrated command measurement at `63cb23d` is later than that CI run.

inventory_review.validation_summary: On 2026-10-19, `tests/run.sh` recorded **212 passed, 0 failed** on `85c1f72609c46ea58e265934272abf52e4889c9e` plus the reviewed working-tree changes (tracked diff SHA-256 `6b1e58659a53475de550108104ba265e752827091e2eb0893ad95783982a7abc`; native binary SHA-256 `6f78739d29acea39800d49948ba71bbf35ad8b887831d60e242ee37021d4f883`). That full run preceded the final Git long-line and package-index byte-verification fixes. The focused checks below passed later that day with those fixes, now committed in the reviewed source above. Their native binary SHA-256 was `25bacd907a13baa8c8a4cbe96f178ae20e4e3cbadd5c902175906b29f65dd5cf`; the package sanitizer check used separately instrumented modules.

inventory_review.validation_limits: The full harness was not rerun after the final focused fixes. These correctness results add no new command timings. Coverage labels identify available fixtures; they do not imply that every referenced suite or conditional branch ran on the reviewed commit. Optional interpreter builds, hardware-dependent paths and credential transitions have their own prerequisites, and this record does not establish current cross-platform or complete CLI conformance.
